Standard sudoku rules apply. Additionally there are four shaded tiles in each 3x3 square, which form a T, L, or S tetromino - each row/column of 3x3 squares has exactly one of each. Also the shaded squares form a valid Nurikabe, i.e. a single connected 'wall' which has no loops, and contains no 2x2 blocks of shaded cells. The shaded numbers in each 3x3 square all sum to 20, but no combination of shaded numbers is used twice.

title: A new type of puzzle from the DASH Mystery Hunt
description:
Here is one of the puzzles from the recent DASH mystery hunt. You can solve the first part in our software: https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/QDnJ2QhNm2 
The rules are: (1) Each region contains one stone, a mass of connected cells (2) Stones from different sectors may not share sides, but can touch at corners (3) If a region contains a number, exactly that many cells must be shaded (4) Half the cells in each column must be shaded (5) If dropped, stones will stack in the bottom half of the grid, completely filling it. Stones will remain intact, keeping their shape, and will not rotate.

title: Sandwich Sudoku:  With A Twist!
description:
You can try Florian Zellmer's puzzle here:

https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/gfn7qnjQrm

Instructions for this puzzle:  Normal Sudoku rules apply.  Clues outside the grid give the sum of the cells "sandwiched" between the 1 and the 9 in the row/column.  HOWEVER the count is always taken starting from the 1 ie you must always count rightwards from the 1 in a row and downwards from a 1 in a column.  If you hit the edge of the grid before finding the 9 then you loop back to the start of the relevant row/column and continue counting.  ie the grid behaves like a torus.

title: How To Solve Slitherlink Puzzles - The Sheep & Wolves Variation
description:
As trailed in our earlier video, here we discuss this beautiful variation on the standard Nikoli Slitherlink puzzle.  For those of you unfamiliar with the rules:

➊ Draw a single closed loop along the grid lines of the diagram which does not visit a grid dot more than once.
 ➋ A number in a cell indicates how many of the grid lines surrounding this cell is used by the loop.
 ➌ For a cell without a number the loop can use any number of surrounding grid lines.
 
Additional Rules for this variation: Cells with circles (sheep) are inside of the loop, cells with crosses (wolves) are outside of the loop.

To play this exact puzzle, please use the line provided by one of our viewers here:

https://pastebin.com/CD6U6V5a

title: Advanced Masyu Puzzle - Viewer Request
description:
We take a look at another Masyu puzzle.  This video also discusses the upcoming video on the Slitherlink variant, Sheep & Wolves.

Masyu rules: draw a single continuous non-intersecting loop that passes through all circled cells. White circles must be travelled straight through, but the loop must turn in the previous and/or next cell in its path.  Black circles must be turned upon, but the loop must travel straight through the next and previous cells in its path.
